specs.anchorText: The standard analogy, from the original paper, is a team of counterfeiters
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette on a clean white background: a friendly cartoon counterfeiter character at a little printing press happily cranking out playful banknotes, while a cheerful cartoon police officer holds one bill up to a magnifying glass, both standing on a curved racetrack-style loop arrow that shows them chasing each other in an endless friendly circle. Neither looks mean; both look determined and a little amused, like rivals who secretly enjoy the game. Soft pastel blues, greens and warm oranges, expressive rounded characters, generous margins, minimal clutter. The style should be friendly and approachable like an XKCD-inspired infographic meets Kurzgesagt. No text or lettering in the image. Keep the composition simple and focused on the chase between the two characters.
specs.alt: A cartoon counterfeiter at a printing press makes fake banknotes while a police officer inspects one with a magnifying glass, the two chasing each other around a looping track to show the generator and discriminator improving in response to one another.
specs.caption: Two rivals who never agreed on anything except that the bank should not be able to tell them apart: the whole chapter is this friendly chase between a forger and a cop.

specs.anchorText: In every model before this chapter, the loss was a fixed formula chosen by a human
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette on a clean white background: on the left, a dusty fixed measuring ruler or stiff old yardstick lying flat and unchanging, representing a hand-written loss function. On the right, a friendly little robot wearing tiny glasses acting as a smart, adaptive judge holding up a flexible measuring tape, leaning in attentively to inspect a small picture, getting visibly sharper-eyed and more alert. An arrow suggests the generator learns by being measured against this living judge rather than the rigid ruler. Soft warm palette, rounded expressive shapes, minimal clutter, generous margins, XKCD-meets-Kurzgesagt style. No text or lettering in the image. Keep one clear visual metaphor: a rigid ruler versus a living, learning judge.
specs.alt: A rigid old ruler on the left contrasts with a friendly robot judge holding a flexible tape measure and squinting attentively at an image on the right, illustrating that a GAN replaces a fixed human-written loss with a second network that learns to measure realism.
specs.caption: Earlier models were graded by a rigid ruler; a GAN hires a living judge who keeps getting better at spotting what fake looks like.

specs.anchorText: Mode collapse is the signature GAN failure
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette on a clean white background: a cartoon factory robot proudly operating a stamping machine that prints an endless line of identical smiling cookies, all exactly the same shape, while a big basket of varied, different-shaped cookies sits ignored and dusty in the corner. The robot looks pleased and a little lazy, having found one safe trick it repeats forever. Gentle humor, no meanness. Soft warm oranges and creams, rounded expressive shapes, minimal clutter, generous margins, XKCD-meets-Kurzgesagt textbook style. No text or lettering in the image. Keep the metaphor focused on producing one identical output over and over while ignoring variety.
specs.alt: A factory robot happily stamps out an endless row of identical cookies while a basket of varied cookie shapes sits ignored in the corner, illustrating mode collapse where a GAN generator produces one safe output forever instead of covering the full diversity of the data.
specs.caption: Mode collapse is a generator that found one trick that works and decided variety was somebody else's problem.

specs.anchorText: where cost is mass times distance moved, hence the name "earth mover"
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette on a clean white background: a cheerful cartoon worker with a wheelbarrow shoveling a pile of dirt from one mound and carrying it across a gap to build up a second mound of the same size, so the two piles match. A faint dotted path with a small distance marker shows the effort of moving the earth. The scene gives a friendly sense that the cost is how much dirt times how far it is carried. Soft warm earthy palette with gentle greens, rounded expressive character, minimal clutter, generous margins, XKCD-meets-Kurzgesagt style. No text or lettering in the image. Keep one clear visual metaphor: moving a pile of earth to match another pile.
specs.alt: A cartoon worker uses a wheelbarrow to move dirt from one mound to reshape it into a matching second mound across a gap, illustrating the Wasserstein earth-mover distance as the cost of transporting mass from the generated distribution to the data distribution.
specs.caption: The Wasserstein distance asks a friendly question a flat divergence cannot: how much dirt, carried how far, to make one pile look like the other.

specs.anchorText: can we control an image at multiple scales, coarse pose separately from fine texture
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette on a clean white background: a tall friendly assembly-line tower or layered control panel building where a cartoon portrait is being built from bottom to top, with a row of labeled-looking dials and sliders down the side, the lower dials controlling the coarse head shape and pose, the middle dials the hair, and the top dials fine skin texture and freckles. A small style-vector character cheerfully turns the knobs at every floor. Each floor adds finer detail to the face. Soft warm pastel palette with purples and greens, rounded shapes, clean and uncluttered, generous margins, XKCD-meets-Kurzgesagt style. No text or lettering in the image. Keep the metaphor focused on per-layer dials controlling different scales of a generated face.
specs.alt: A layered tower builds a cartoon portrait floor by floor, with dials down the side where lower dials set coarse pose and head shape and upper dials set fine texture and freckles, while a style-vector character turns a knob at every level, illustrating StyleGAN injecting a style at each layer for scale-separated control.
specs.caption: Inject the style once and you get a black box; inject it at every floor and you get a dial for pose, a dial for hair, and a dial for freckles.

specs.anchorText: if you translate an image to the other domain and back, you should recover the original
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette on a clean white background: a friendly cartoon painter character paints black stripes onto a cheerful horse to turn it into a zebra, then in a return arrow washes the stripes off with a sponge to recover the exact same horse in the exact same pose and background. Show it as a gentle round-trip loop with two arrows, emphasizing that the horse comes back unchanged except for the stripes. Warm friendly palette, expressive rounded characters, minimal clutter, generous margins, XKCD-meets-Kurzgesagt style. No text or lettering in the image. Keep the metaphor focused on the reversible there-and-back translation between a horse and a zebra.
specs.alt: A cartoon painter adds stripes to a horse to make a zebra and then washes them off with a sponge to recover the identical horse in the same pose, illustrating CycleGAN's cycle-consistency loss that a translation you can undo and get the original back is a translation you can trust.
specs.caption: Cycle consistency is the rule that if you paint the stripes on, you had better be able to wash them off and get the very same horse back.
